cover letter
Red Cross Adult CPR and First Aid Certification (Preferred)
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, the Associate Director of Member Services oversees the entire Member Services unit within the Department of Recreation & Wellbeing. The Associate Director of Member Services establishes core goals, strategic priorities, and culture for both patron engagement and staff operations across member experience and customer sales. This position manages full unit operations, including high-level escalated decision-making, service quality governance, software ownership, systems integration, and administrative functions spanning finance, human resources, and IT. The Associate Director of Member Services demonstrates seasoned judgment in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions, setting workload expectations, resolving staff priorities and conflicts, and ensuring seamless operations across all departmental spaces.
Direct Supervision and Leadership of Member Services - 25%
Provides direct supervision, coaching, and strategic direction to two direct reports:
(1) the Assistant Director of Customer Service, who oversees business operations, sales, passport operations, program registrations, memberships, and locker rentals; and
(2) the Assistant Director of Member Experience, who focuses on the human element, supervising facility leadership student staff and managing administrative data entry.

Oversees recruitment, onboarding, training, performance management, and workforce development across the entire Member Services area. Provides indirect supervision to 7FTE in Member Services (direct reports of each Assistant Director).
Culture, Member Service Governance, and Prioritization - 20%
Sets the core goals, priorities, and cultural expectations for both patrons entering facility spaces and staff working in customer sales and member experience.
Governs service assessments and defines key metrics to answer: "How do we measure success for this area?"

Defines Area and Unit KPIs and standards for customer service, including response times, ticket resolution, task expectations, and ongoing priorities. Advocates for and manages workload pivoting, ensuring staff understand when administrative tasks must yield to high-touch, in-person experiences.
Step in to enforce SOPs and resolve conflict or confusion regarding priorities within the Member Services team.
Serves as the primary resource and lead for all RecWell software needs, partnering closely with Health & Wellbeing IT.
Acts as the functional software owner for all Member Services software applications, including Fusion, CampDoc, Connect2, staff scheduling systems, density monitors, and WaitWell.
Directs application administration, system implementation, data integrity, and administrative data entry workflows across member services systems.
Provides reports, metrics, and trend analysis to other department areas to inform data-driven decisions and support cross-program success.
Financial Management - 15%
Oversees financial management, budget preparation, recharge administration, and revenue generation strategies for customer-facing services.
Analyzes financial reports, performs trend studies, and evaluates resource utilization for membership sales, passport operations, locker rentals, and program registrations.
Campus and Divisional Leadership - 5%
Represents the department on campus-wide and divisional committees, working groups, and initiatives.
Serves as a key liaison across university partners to align Member Services practices with broader institutional goals.

Establishes and governs policies, procedures, and protocols for recreation spaces and customer interactions to ensure full compliance with campus mandates, risk management standards, and regulatory policies (including CANRA and activities involving minors).
Handles escalated user conflicts, policy violations, and risk mitigation strategies.
Inter-Unit Alignment and Escalated Collaboration - 5%
Partners with other Associate Directors to set workload support expectations and ensure alignment across departments.
Serves as the escalation point and lead for inter-unit projects, cross-functional strategies, and joint departmental initiatives.
Other duties as assigned - 5%
Thorough knowledge of and/or ability to learn University rules and regulations, processes, protocols and procedures for budget, account and fund management, personnel management.
Thorough knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques, human resources policies and procedures for staff and academic employees.

In-depth knowledge of and/or ability to learn member services software applications and systems (e.g., Fusion, CampDoc, Connect2, staff scheduling tools, density monitors, WaitWell) and ability to partner with divisional IT.
Strong skills in establishing customer service standards, governance metrics, SOP creation, and service assessment evaluation.
Proven capability to resolve interpersonal conflict, manage workload prioritization, and foster a positive culture for patrons and staff.
Advanced skills in short- and long-term planning, analysis, problem-solving, and conflict resolution.
Interpersonal communication skills including verbal, written, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and counseling skills.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
